The following table provides information about the effective tax rate:

The lower effective tax rate for the third quarter of 2026 compared to the third quarter of 2025 was primarily driven by lower income before tax resulting from the AFS securities repositioning, which increased the relative benefit of tax credits, renewable energy tax credit investing activity, and other tax-advantaged items on the effective tax rate. The provision for income taxes was also impacted by the RAC loan sale and AFS securities repositioning.

net.text: For the third quarter of 2026, we reported net income of $684 million, or $0.56 per diluted share, which reflects the impact of several actions to better position Truist for the future. The actions described below simplify the Company, allow us to focus more on our core businesses, and further strengthen our balance sheet by reducing credit risk, interest rate risk, and wholesale funding.

Net interest income.heading: Net Interest Income
Net interest income.text:
Three Months Ended September 30, 2026 compared to the Three Months Ended September 30, 2025

Net interest income - TE increased $27 million, or 0.7%, compared to the third quarter of 2025, driven primarily by fixed-rate asset and liability repricing, higher client deposit balances, and higher loan balances, partially offset by lower loan spreads and unfavorable deposit mix. NIM - TE was 3.00%, stable compared to the third quarter of 2025.

• Average earning assets increased $5.4 billion, or 1.1%, primarily due to an increase in average total loans of $7.4 billion, or 2.3%.

• The yield on the average total loan portfolio was 5.71%, down 29 basis points. The yield on the average securities portfolio was 3.03%, down 13 basis points.

• Average deposits increased $14.1 billion, or 3.6%, average short-term borrowings decreased $8.2 billion, or 31%, and average long-term debt increased $3.7 billion, or 8.9%.

• The average cost of total deposits was 1.59%, down 25 basis points. The average cost of short-term borrowings was 3.96%, down 46 basis points.

Noninterest income.heading: Noninterest Income
Noninterest income.text:
Noninterest income is a significant driver of Truist’s financial results. The Company has diversified its sources of revenue to reduce its reliance on traditional spread-based interest income, as certain fee-based activities are a relatively stable revenue source during periods of changing interest rates. The following table provides the components of Truist’s noninterest income:

Noninterest income decreased $1.5 billion for the third quarter of 2026 compared to the third quarter of 2025, and $1.1 billion for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 compared to 2025. The third quarter of 2026 included losses from AFS securities sales of $1.4 billion and losses associated with the RAC loan sale of $66 million (other income).

For the three months ended September 30, 2026:

• Wealth management income increased primarily reflecting favorable market performance.

• Other income decreased primarily due to the losses associated with the RAC loan sale and lower returns from investments held for post-retirement benefits (which were offset by lower personnel expense).

intro.text: Truist Financial Corporation is a purpose-driven financial services company committed to inspiring and building better lives and communities. Headquartered in Charlotte, North Carolina, Truist has leading market share in many of the high-growth markets in the U.S. and offers a wide range of products and services through its WB and CSBB operating segments, including consumer and small business banking, commercial and corporate banking, investment banking and capital markets, wealth management, payments, and specialized lending businesses. Refer to the “Segment Results” section in MD&A and “Note 21. Operating Segments” for additional information on the Company’s reportable segments.
